name: Bristol Whitebeam
grown_as: A native tree found wild only in the Avon Gorge, Bristol (formerly Sorbus bristoliensis). Grown here as a young garden tree.
habit: A small deciduous tree, 6 to 10 m when old, with a compact, rounded crown on upright branches. Smooth grey bark. In a garden, a young tree with a single straight stem.

leaf.outline: Obovate to diamond-shaped (rhombic), widest at or a little above the middle, 6 to 9 cm long, about two-thirds as wide
leaf.margin: Shallow, forward-pointing lobes, deepest around the middle of the leaf and fading out towards the tip; each lobe edged with small sharp teeth. The wedge base has no lobes or teeth
leaf.veins: A midrib and 7 to 9 pairs of straight, parallel side veins, each running out to a lobe
leaf.surface: Glossy bright green above; grey-green felt beneath (greyer and thinner than the snow-white felt of common whitebeam)
leaf.colour: Bright green above, grey-green beneath; yellow-brown in autumn

flower.form: Small open flowers in a flat-topped head
flower.petals: Five, free, round to oval, spreading
flower.centre: About twenty stamens with cream to pinkish anthers around two or three styles
flower.carried: Many together in dense, flat-topped, branched clusters (corymbs) 6 to 10 cm across at the ends of short shoots, held upright above the leaves

fruit: Small pomes, round to slightly oval, 8 to 12 mm, ripening bright orange (some orange-pink), with a few small pale dots (lenticels) and the dried sepals at the tip. In upright to drooping bunches on felted stalks. September to October. Fruit set: bunches of small green berries in the old flower heads.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as a bought tree
winter: Bare tree with smooth grey bark. Fat, egg-shaped green buds with brown-edged scales and a tuft of grey wool at the tip.

leaf: leaf widest about the middle with a long untoothed wedge base
shallow toothed lobes deepest at the middle, fading to the tip
7 to 9 pairs of straight parallel veins
grey-green felt beneath if the back shows
bloom: a cluster of pale stamens in the centre
part of a flat-topped head of many flowers
young: shallowly lobed leaves with grey undersides
dormant: bare tree with smooth grey bark
fat green buds with brown-edged scales
flower: flat-topped white flower heads at the shoot tips
heads held up above shallowly lobed leaves
set: bunches of small green berries in the old flower heads
crop: bunches of small bright orange berries

look_alikes: Common whitebeam (Sorbus aria) has unlobed leaves with snow-white undersides and scarlet berries. Swedish whitebeam (Scandosorbus intermedia) has more deeply lobed leaves with yellow-grey felt and red berries. The Avon Gorge has several other rare whitebeams, such as Wilmott's and Leigh Woods whitebeams, which differ in leaf shape, felt colour and fruit colour; Bristol whitebeam is the one with orange fruit. Wild service tree has deeply and sharply lobed leaves that are green beneath, with brown fruit. Rowan has feather-like compound leaves.
